title: Jay-Z Sold Half Of One Brand For $300 Million

beats.say: In 2021, Jay-Z cashed out half of his champagne brand for an estimated three hundred million dollars.
beats.visual: a dark champagne bottle with a metallic gold surface on black glass, hard rim light, no text, no people

beats.say: The brand is Ace of Spades. He took full ownership of it in twenty fourteen.
beats.visual: a dim private cellar of dusty bottles lined in rows under a single hanging bulb, no people

beats.say: He wanted to own a brand, not just promote one.
beats.visual: a spotlit empty stage with a single microphone stand and a row of dark seats, no people

beats.say: In twenty nineteen it sold half a million bottles.
beats.visual: a towering wall of wooden shipping crates in a vast warehouse at night, cold sodium light

beats.say: So what is half of a growing brand worth to the right buyer?
beats.visual: a pair of old brass scales balanced with gold on one side, dramatic dark background

beats.say: According to the Financial Times, in February twenty twenty one he sold fifty percent to Moet Hennessy. The price was not disclosed.
beats.visual: two heavy glass doors of a corporate tower opening in a bright lobby at dawn, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Forbes valued the brand near six hundred and thirty million dollars. That is an estimate, not a filing.
beats.visual: a handwritten ledger page with columns of numbers under a green banker lamp, close-up

beats.say: He kept the other half, and a seat at the table.
beats.visual: a long dark conference table with one chair pulled out and the rest pushed in, moody light

beats.say: And it was not a fluke: days later, Square agreed to pay two hundred and ninety seven million dollars for most of Tidal.
beats.visual: a glowing tower of server racks in a dark data hall, blue light, no people

beats.say: Why does it matter? Ownership turns a name into an asset you can sell.
beats.visual: a rising staircase of coins under a spotlight, climbing into darkness

beats.say: The honest catch. He started with a hit record and famous partners, and many of his other businesses never became giants.
beats.visual: a row of locked shop shutters on a dark city street at night, one with light behind it

beats.say: Your takeaway is not to build a brand. It is to ask, in every deal, what part of this can I own?
beats.visual: a hand holding a single brass key up to the light, extreme close-up, no face

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Jay-Z sold half of Ace of Spades to Moet Hennessy in 2021. Forbes estimated at least $300 million in cash. What owning the brand did, and the catch. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Jay-Z took full ownership of Armand de Brignac in 2014 and sold 50% to Moet Hennessy in 2021. Forbes estimated at least $300 million in cash. The ownership lesson and the honest catch.
first_comment: Would you rather be paid to promote a brand or own part of it? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: Full ownership of Armand de Brignac (Ace of Spades) in 2014; 500,000 bottles sold in 2019
2021-02-22 sold 50% to Moet Hennessy (LVMH), price undisclosed
Forbes estimated brand at about $630M and his cash at least $300M (estimate)
Tidal: Square agreed to pay $297M in cash and stock for a significant majority stake, March 2021
Catch: started with a hit record and famous partners; valuations are estimates
